paper_title: Knowledge Crosswords Geometric Knowledge Reasoning with Large Language   Models
caption: Problem distribution based on the correctness under the w/ knowledge and w/o knowledge settings using Zero-Shot.
model_annotation: The figure presents three pie charts—labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard”—showing the distribution of problem outcomes under Zero-Shot evaluation, categorized by whether the model had access to knowledge (N+K+) or not (N–K+, N–K–, N+K–), as indicated in the legend. In the “easy” chart, the largest segment (55.4%, teal) corresponds to correct answers with knowledge (N+K+), followed by 38.3% (yellow) for correct without knowledge (N–K+), 4.6% (orange) for incorrect without knowledge (N–K–), and 1.7% (red) for incorrect with knowledge (N+K–). The “medium” chart shows a similar pattern: 58.8% (teal, N+K+), 35.4% (yellow, N–K+), 4.0% (orange, N–K–), and 1.8% (red, N+K–). In the “hard” chart, the proportions shift: 37.3% (yellow, N–K+), 37.9% (orange, N–K–), 18.1% (teal, N+K+), and 6.7% (red, N+K–), indicating that without knowledge, performance is more evenly split between correct and incorrect, while with knowledge, success rates drop significantly compared to easier problems. All charts include percentage labels within each slice and share a common legend positioned to the right.
